unresolved_items: CONTRADICTION, not a clean result: 69 package-manager install command line(s) ran in the window and DeviceNetworkEvents recorded 0 tarball fetches. Package downloads are therefore not observable on this table, so matching against 2,208 specs could not have found anything and this vector must not be read as clean. Package-registry hosts actually seen in the window: registry.npmjs.org (14 rows, 0 tarball-like). Cause, measured rather than inferred: 3 of 5 installing device(s) (macOS, 59 of 69 install command lines) produced DeviceNetworkEvents rows in the window with RemoteUrl empty on every one, so no URL - malicious or benign - could have been recorded for the traffic those installs generated. On the 2 device(s) that do populate RemoteUrl, the npmjs rows carry the hostname with no path, so the '<name>/-/<name>-<version>.tgz' segment this check matches on cannot appear there either. A mirror is therefore NOT the explanation: the connection to the registry was recorded, only the path was not. Ours to close, and it is a configuration change rather than an access request: enable Defender Network Protection in block or audit mode on macOS and Linux, which is the feature that populates RemoteUrl with a full URL on those platforms. Until then, per-package install attribution on endpoints is unavailable and the lockfile and Actions vectors carry this question alone.

2,670 lifecycle-script execution(s) ran on 101 device(s) in the window (install.js / install.cjs and similar), none carrying a campaign artifact name. None can be attributed to a package: DeviceProcessEvents records the command line 'node install.cjs' and the parent shell, but not the working directory, so the node_modules path that would name the package is absent. These executions are the lifecycle vector this worm uses, and they are neither cleared nor implicated. Ours to close by reading InitiatingProcessFolderPath against a package manifest on the named devices, which is host-side work rather than a query.

coverage_gaps.gap: DeviceNetworkEvents.RemoteUrl carries no path on the platforms that install npm packages, so tarball-level install attribution is impossible on endpoints
coverage_gaps.population: 3 of 5 device(s) that ran a package-manager install in the window (macOS), carrying 59 of 69 install command line(s). Those devices produced DeviceNetworkEvents rows with RemoteUrl empty on every one.
coverage_gaps.named_by: the per-device rows of the installer_devices query in this artifact (evidence.installer_devices.rows), each carrying DeviceName, OSPlatform, InstallCmds and UrlRows - so the devices needing the configuration change can be listed by name without re-running the hunt.
coverage_gaps.cannot_confirm_or_deny: which package and which version any of those install command lines actually fetched. The malicious-spec match runs on the tarball path segment '<name>/-/<name>-<version>.tgz', and that segment is absent from every row, so a zero here is untested rather than clean.
coverage_gaps.closed_by: Enable Defender Network Protection (audit mode is sufficient) on macOS and Linux endpoints. Not a permission gap - ThreatHunting.Read.All already returns these tables; the column is empty at the source.
coverage_gaps.owner: Endpoint security - the team that owns the Defender device configuration profiles for macOS and Linux
coverage_gaps._correction: Field names normalized in place on 2026-08-10 to the coverage-gap contract (gap, population, named_by, cannot_confirm_or_deny, closed_by, owner). The collector emitted 'closes_it' and 'measured' only; scripts/hunt/hunt_install_activity.py now emits the full set, so the next run reproduces this shape without patching. No measured value was changed - population, named_by and cannot_confirm_or_deny are derived from the 'measured' block and the installer_devices rows already in this file.

bound_summary._how_to_read_this: If the latest publish sits well inside the bracket, the bracket is not the thing bounding it and the close time is a registry fact. If it sits at the bracket edge, widen the bracket again before reporting a close.
